clue.text: Play is not to exhaust Daisy and Holly, say

parts.note: Daisy is a stock name for a cow; to under-milk her is to stop short of draining her udder
holly is a tree, so it is an example of wood

explanation.surface: Someone resolves not to wear out two girls named Daisy and Holly during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy and Holly read as two girls' names; Daisy is the cow and Holly the tree. The answer is Dylan Thomas's radio play about a Welsh village.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas wrote this famous 'play for voices', so it is a specific example of a drama.

clue.text: In immoderate battle, I captured one of the colours

parts.note: ultra as a prefix or noun means extreme, beyond moderation

indicators.note: the battle takes the letter I prisoner, so it goes inside the word

parts.note: the Marne was the river of two great First World War battles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier boasts of taking a regimental colour in a fierce battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The colours' are a regiment's flags in the surface, but the definition means a shade of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a vivid deep blue pigment, originally ground from lapis lazuli, so it is one shade among many.

clue.text: Nobbled, taking up shell

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking the word up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to de-pod peas is to take them out of their pods, which is shelling them

explanation.surface: A racehorse has been got at, and someone is collecting shell cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Nobbled is British racing slang for drugging a horse to stop it winning. 'Taking up' sounds like collecting; in a down clue it means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A doped horse has been given drugs, which is exactly what nobbling one means in racing slang.

clue.text: Tape needs tying again

parts.note: re- is the prefix that means doing something once more
cording is binding something with cord

explanation.surface: A parcel's tape has come loose and wants knotting again.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as re-cording, the word means tying with cord again.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape is a recording of sound or pictures, as in a cassette or video, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Encroach on one motorway, say — quickly run over

indicators.note: turned over, the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the usual abbreviation for 'for example', which is what say means here
to nip is to dash somewhere briefly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A driver trespasses on a motorway lane and then dashes across it.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in the order say, quickly run, motorway, one, then the lot is reversed. 'On' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge on something is to have an effect that intrudes upon it, a near synonym of trespass.

clue.text: Leaders Lynn may follow in college

definitions.meaning: monarchs are rulers, the heads of their nations
... Lynn is a market town in Norfolk, England
... College is found at both Cambridge and London

explanation.surface: Heads of a college might be led by someone called Lynn.
explanation.walkthrough: Lynn looks like a person's name; it is the second word of the Norfolk town King's Lynn.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchs are rulers, and the same word with an apostrophe opens the names King's Lynn and King's College.

clue.text: Protestant, a person of no latitude?

parts.note: O is the figure nought, so it stands for no or nothing
latitude in the sense of scope or freedom is range
man is used for a person in general

explanation.surface: A Protestant is mocked as someone allowed no freedom at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Latitude suggests geography; here it means scope. An Orangeman belongs to the Orange Order, a Protestant society in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order, founded to honour William of Orange, are by definition committed Protestants.

clue.text: Fail one's cast

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cube thrown in games

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' tempts as actors in a play; it is the throw of a dice cube.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for collapsing or expiring and a noun for the single cube of a pair of dice.

clue.text: Up in theatre?

definitions.meaning: the answer means up on top of something
split into two short words, the answer places a patient at an operation, which is where an operating theatre puts you

explanation.walkthrough: Theatre looks like the stage; it is the hospital's operating theatre, and at op is where a patient in it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on top of, so it is a positional synonym for being high above something.

clue.text: City below Wellington

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital of Denmark
second meaning: the Duke of Wellington's horse, which carried him at Waterloo

explanation.walkthrough: Wellington tempts as the New Zealand capital, so a city to its south; it is the Duke, and below him was his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish capital shares its name with the chestnut stallion the Duke rode throughout the Battle of Waterloo.

clue.text: Chap's boldness failing at last, meeting bureaucrat

parts.note: a chap is a man; the 's joins him to what follows

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for boldness gives out and drops away

parts.note: daring is courage or audacity

explanation.surface: A man's courage deserts him just as he faces an official.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the informal word for a powerful senior civil servant, after the officials of imperial China.

clue.text: Showed exasperation with pronounced arrogance

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for arrogance gives the answer's sound

parts.note: side is an old slang word for swagger or putting on airs

explanation.surface: Someone shows irritation in a markedly haughty manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' reads as 'marked'; it is the sound signal. Side, meaning conceit, is chiefly British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To let out a long audible breath is the classic gesture of weariness or irritation.

clue.text: Carved limestone, so cold

indicators.note: the stone is cut into a new shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sculpture cut from limestone feels chilly to the touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold looks like the temperature of stone; it describes a person without feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold person shows no feeling, which is exactly what lacking emotion describes.

clue.text: Quality of quilt, perhaps, but not of blanket cover

definitions.meaning: a patchwork quilt is made of many separate patches
blanket cover is complete coverage, the opposite of uneven or spotty

explanation.walkthrough: Blanket and quilt read as bedding; blanket cover also means coverage that is total, the very opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unevenness, being in patches here and there, describes a patchwork quilt but not complete coverage.

clue.text: Classy setting in which to find lobster?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a setting of class: the taxonomic class an animal is grouped in
lobsters belong to the class of crabs, shrimps and their kin

explanation.walkthrough: Classy setting suggests an upmarket restaurant serving lobster; it means the biological class.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists group lobsters, crabs and shrimps in this hard-shelled arthropod group of the animal kingdom.

clue.text: Cantor started this fixed idea

parts.note: set means fixed or firmly established
a theory is an idea put forward to explain something

explanation.surface: A synagogue cantor began some obsession of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: A cantor leads singing in a synagogue; here it is Georg Cantor, the mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Cantor founded this branch of mathematics dealing with collections of objects and infinite sizes.

clue.text: Indicative maybe of turning fate

indicators.note: turning the word round means reading it backwards

parts.note: doom is one's grim destiny

explanation.surface: Something hints that fortune is about to change.
explanation.walkthrough: Indicative looks like an adjective meaning 'suggestive'; it is the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the indicative is one verb mood, alongside the subjunctive and imperative, so it is an example.

clue.text: One name held by Australia's first characters: aborigines

indicators.note: the two letters are clasped inside the pair from Australia

parts.note: the opening two letters of the country's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A note about the names of Australia's original inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: The Australian setting points at Aboriginal Australians; the answer is Japan's indigenous people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ainu are the indigenous native people of Hokkaido and northern Japan.

clue.text: Splendid to receive money — excellent support for scholarship

indicators.note: the word for splendid takes in the other pieces, which sit inside it

parts.note: grand means magnificent or impressive
tin is old British slang for cash
A1 means first-rate, and the 1 is written as an I

explanation.surface: A scholar is delighted to get a fine sum of money in support.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant-in-aid is a sum given by a public body to fund a project, such as a student's study.

clue.text: Successful at stringing lover along, she ran a 7 ragged

definitions.text: Successful at stringing lover along, she

indicators.note: run ragged, worn to tatters, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: the answer to 7-down, DIE

explanation.surface: A woman who kept her lover on a string led him a merry chase.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread to find his way out of the Minotaur's labyrinth, so she literally strung her lover along. '7' stands for the answer to 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ariadne's thread let Theseus escape the labyrinth, a playful take on leading a lover on.

clue.text: Digestive tract finally put on record in film

indicators.note: the record and letter go inside the film

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: the letter is placed onto the end of the record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the last letter of tract is taken

parts.note: the word whose closing letter is taken

explanation.surface: A film documents the digestive system, with a recording of the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: Digestive tract reads as one phrase; the definition is only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Peptic is the medical adjective for things relating to digestion, as in a peptic ulcer.

clue.text: Climber's aid not on? That can be painful

indicators.note: the word on is to be absent from the climber's aid

parts.note: a crampon is a spiked frame fixed to a boot for climbing on ice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber's equipment is not fitted, which could hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a sudden painful muscle spasm, often met in the legs after exertion.

clue.text: Cruel and silly to screen a Pooh production

indicators.note: the word for silly hides the other piece within it

parts.note: inane means pointless or foolish
Winnie-the-Pooh composes little songs he calls hums

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it cruel and silly to show a Winnie-the-Pooh film.
explanation.walkthrough: Screen and production suggest a film; Pooh's songs are hums in A. A. Milne's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane describes behaviour lacking compassion, so it is a close synonym of heartless.

clue.text: Plan article in French: a lot of these in Canada

definitions.text: a lot of these in Canada

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart of an area
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A note on planning an article in French about a Canadian subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Article tempts as a piece of writing; it is the grammatical word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada has many of these trees, and their leaf is on the national flag.

clue.text: Uncertain batter caught on boundaries of outfield

definitions.meaning: first meaning: precarious, with the outcome in doubt

definitions.text: batter caught on boundaries of outfield
definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: a batter who just edges the ball and must leave, caught out by a fielder at the boundary

explanation.surface: A hesitant cricket batter is caught at the edge of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who gets the slightest touch on the ball and is caught has to go; the phrase for that moment also means a close-run thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation whose outcome is risky and could go either way.

clue.text: Monster's limitless violence

indicators.note: without its limits, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: force is physical violence or compulsion

explanation.surface: A monster's violence knows no bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An orc is a brutish goblin creature of folklore and Tolkien's fantasy fiction.

clue.text: Request fold to be trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed like a hem, the word loses its end

parts.note: a pleat is a fold sewn into cloth

explanation.surface: A dressmaker is asked to shorten a fold in a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal, so it is a synonym of an entreaty.

clue.text: Church maps out one diocese and others, in a way, overseas

indicators.note: the word maps comes out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire
sees are bishops' dioceses, so other ones are sees

explanation.surface: A church charts one diocese and several more, as part of a mission abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' is a road; the avenue is in Paris, so overseas from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous Parisian avenue running from the Place de la Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe.
